B. -1.48

D. -1.50

At transport step 10, the infilling solution has moved through the column. Given the exchange capacity of 0.001 moles and the infilling $\text{Na}^+$ concentration of 1.0 mmol/kgw, the retardation factor for the $\text{Na}^+$ front is approximately $R = 1 + (\Delta q / \Delta c) = 1 + (0.001 / 0.001) = 2$. After 10 shifts, the front has moved 5 cells ($10/2$). Thus, cell 4 is entirely behind the exchange front and is occupied by the infilling solution (nearly pure $\text{NaCl}$ solution at 1.0 mmol/kgw).
